title: The UK Power Grid Has a Phantom Data Center Problem
summary:
In July, the UK’s energy regulator, Ofgem, laid out a proposal meant to force phantom data centers out of the swollen queue.
Data center developers face delays almost everywhere; similar grid congestion issues afflict the US and countries across Europe.
The frenzied data center buildout “is bringing a huge amount of capital investment into the UK,” says Alex Burgoyne, head of data centers at real estate consultancy Knight Frank.
New data centers make up 73 gigawatts of that—equivalent to one and a half times the peak demand for the entire UK last year—and counting.
“No one really understands … what the real grid demand will be because of these phantom projects.”The crowded queue is largely the product of an incentives problem.

summary:
TL;DR Varun Datta, Web3 venture capitalist and CEO of Truth Ventures, explores how AI agents gaining the ability to transact independently could accelerate the emerging machine economy and create new opportunities for investors.
AI agents are getting wallets and are now able to make decisions on behalf of owners.
The biggest news is the launch of Cloudflare Wallets on August 4, 2026.
As part of its agents week, it gives AI agents running on its network a stablecoin balance and a readable identity to present when paying for APIs, data, and content.
“AI agents need to transact with counterparties they haven’t met at times when traditional banks are not open and settle without any reversal.

title: Japan wants stock and bond settlement to happen instantly, on a blockchain
summary:
Portions of the balances banks hold at the Bank of Japan would be converted into digital tokens on a blockchain network, making this an interbank central bank digital currency rather than anything consumers would touch.
Settlement infrastructure is the sort of thing that has to work on the first day and every day afterwards.
Officials want to keep Japanese markets competitive as the United States and Europe build out tokenised securities infrastructure, which is a defensive framing rather than an ambition to lead.
Japan has formed here, having run digital currency experiments through the Bank of Japan for several years without committing to a retail launch.
Japan proposing to tokenise central bank money rather than the securities themselves is a version of that argument.

title: Anthropic wants investors to believe its ‘total addressable market’ is worth $30 trillion—nearly the size of the entire US economy
summary:
Now come total addressable market estimates—known as TAMs—worth roughly 40% of the entire US equity market.

AI lab Anthropic, reportedly on the verge of a $2 trillion IPO, is preparing to tell investors that its total addressable market is worth more than $30 trillion, according to a report in the Wall Street Journal.
Rather than a forecast of Anthropic's imminent sales, a total addressable market, or TAM, is the annual revenue a company could theoretically generate if it captured 100% of the relevant market.

title: Plaud is launching AI earbuds
summary:
Plaud has introduced a new AI wearable that’s designed to record, transcribe, and summarize your conversations, only this time it looks like earbuds instead of a pin.
The Plaud One Explorer Edition can be worn like traditional earbuds or used through its standalone charging case, and the case includes built-in 4G to upload and process conversations without relying on your phone or Wi-Fi to stay connected.
They can record for up to six hours according to Plaud, which is also the maximum estimated battery life.
Here’s what the charging case looks like.
Image: PlaudThe Plaud One costs $249.99 and is available to preorder “in selected markets” starting today, with shipping expected to start in Q4, 2026.

title: South Korea’s regulator says Meta’s teen limits should apply everywhere, not just America
summary:
South Korea’s media regulator has said that Meta’s new protections for young users should ideally apply worldwide rather than only in the markets that forced them, which is a modest-sounding statement with a substantial ask inside it.
The measures in question come from Meta’s settlement with US state attorneys general, and the company has already signalled that they do not travel automatically.
The Korea Media and Communications Commission said in a statement that social media providers needed to take greater responsibility for protecting minors.
It also pointed out that seven bills aimed at strengthening youth protection on social platforms are currently sitting in the National Assembly.
What Meta agreed to in the United States is unusually specific for a settlement of this kind.

title: What We Still Don’t Know About OpenAI’s Hugging Face Hack
summary:
Hugging Face initially disclosed the incident on July 16 without naming the culprit; five days later, OpenAI acknowledged that its own agents were responsible.
OpenAI’s postmortem has been eagerly awaited by AI researchers and policymakers hoping to prevent AI agents from causing similar kinds of real-world harm.
After the Hugging Face hack was first disclosed, attorneys general from 15 states sent a letter to OpenAI asking it to preserve evidence about it.
As part of OpenAI’s investigation, the company allowed two independent research groups, METR and Redwood Research, to audit the Hugging Face hack.
Those groups also released their independent report on Wednesday, which found that more than 700 AI agents were part of the Hugging Face breach—far more than had previously been revealed.

title: AI Slop Is Ruining Cute Animals on the Internet
summary:
AI-generated videos and pictures are destroying one of the largest and most enduring sources of joy and compassion on the internet: animals.
The explosion of deepfakes and AI slop over the past few years has led to widespread frustration among viewers, creators, and organizations that support animals, forcing everyone to hunt in the pixels for glitches or other telltale signs of AI.
A disheartened Butler didn’t pay up.
In the past, people have claimed We Animals’ work is staged or photoshopped.
But for the owners of AI slop accounts, synthetic imagery can be a convenient path to collecting likes and ad revenue.

title: A Judge Has Blocked the Pentagon’s Attempt to Blacklist Anthropic
summary:
A federal judge on Thursday barred the Trump administration from designating Anthropic a national security risk over a dispute about the use of its AI models, ruling that the designation amounted to unconstitutional retaliation.
The judge also ruled that nine agencies—including the Pentagon, the Treasury Department, the State Department, and the Department of Homeland Security—had improperly imposed sanctions on Anthropic.
In a statement, Anthropic spokesperson Danielle Cohen said, “We welcome the court’s ruling that this supply-chain risk designation was unlawful.
Anthropic’s top AI models are considered some of the best in the world.
Lin cited the administration’s involvement in reviewing advanced Anthropic models as part of her ruling.

title: The Humanoids at China’s Robot Games Were Faster Than Usain Bolt—but I’m More Impressed by Their Tweezer Mastery
summary:
If you’re anything like me, the World Humanoid Robot Games are a highlight of your sporting calendar.
The opening ceremony showcased the sheer size of the event—the organizers say that more than 600 teams showed up with over 2,000 robots.
There are more than 100 humanoid robot manufacturers in China alone, and participants also traveled in from 15 other countries.
Humanoid robots are seen preparing for the opening ceremony of the World Humanoid Robot Games.
Witness the Tiangong Ultra, developed by the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation ​Center, running the 100-meter dash in 8.86 seconds.

title: VC Founder Says Product Managers Will Be in Demand in the AI Era
summary:
Nicolas Sauvage believes judgment and taste will be what sets people apart in the AI era — and that's why he's bullish on product managers.
The president of venture capital firm TDK Ventures told Business Insider that product managers are one of three job categories that will rise in demand as AI reshapes work.
Founded in 2019 by Sauvage, TDK Ventures manages $500 million across four funds and invests in tech entrepreneurs.
Product managers also understand what customers want and how to turn those insights into products and solutions that are compelling and competitive, he said.
Engineers now often think more like product managers, while product managers can build features and test their own demos.

title: Independent project franchising: why big software companies should spin out innovation instead of killing it
summary:
TL;DR Large software companies routinely build internal tools that prove valuable, then let them decay when priorities shift.
My argument is simple: when a useful internal project no longer fits the corporate roadmap, companies should consider giving it independence before they abandon it.
Software engineers know the pattern.
Deloitte’s 2026 Global Software Industry Outlook says software creation is becoming faster and cheaper, while lean AI-native challengers are pressuring established companies.
My own move from corporate software development into independent product building changed how I see this problem.

title: Boston Scientific has disclosed a cybersecurity incident causing a global disruption to operations
summary:
Boston Scientific has told the US Securities and Exchange Commission that a cybersecurity incident detected on 25 August has caused “a global disruption to the Company’s operations”, including its ability to process and ship customer orders.
Boston Scientific makes pacemakers, stents, catheters, and neuromodulation devices, so an interruption to shipping is not an administrative inconvenience but a supply problem for hospitals with procedures scheduled.
Boston Scientific manufactures implantable hardware with remote monitoring, and while nothing in the filing suggests those systems were touched, the filing does not say they were not.
These are manufacturers with global supply chains, low tolerance for downtime, and customers who cannot simply wait, which is the profile extortion operations look for.
Boston Scientific says it is working to restore affected systems without saying when, and until orders are moving, the material impact question again answers itself a little more each day.

title: AI won’t transform healthcare until we fix information overload
summary:
Artificial intelligence will only improve healthcare if it protects clinical attention rather than adding another layer of complexity.
Working alongside healthcare organizations implementing AI has made one lesson impossible to ignore: the biggest challenge is no longer access to information.
This distinction is essential because discussions about healthcare AI often focus on whether machines will replace professionals.
Healthcare organizations must ensure that clinicians understand how AI systems reach recommendations and when those recommendations should be questioned.
The State of Healthcare IT 2026 Report from SolvEdge found that healthcare organizations are deploying clinical AI tools faster than they are developing governance frameworks to manage them.

title: Barret Zoph is going back to Google, six years and two startups later
summary:
Barret Zoph is joining Google DeepMind as vice president of research, returning to the organisation he spent six years in before it was DeepMind at all.
Google Brain merged with DeepMind in 2023, so the organisation he is rejoining is not quite the one he left.
That is arguably what DeepMind needs more of if it is being pulled towards Gemini product cycles.
Neither Zoph nor Google has said much about what he will actually work on.
Whether Zoph stays longer than the roughly eighteen months he gave Thinking Machines is the question his last few moves invite.

title: JPMorgan leads a $5B debt package for Volta’s AI data centre buildout
summary:
JPMorgan has begun approaching lenders about a $5B debt package to fund Volta Infra Holdings’ AI data centre buildout, weeks after the seven-month-old company raised $300M at a $2.4B valuation.
Its first major site is a 121-megawatt campus in Norway leased from bitcoin miner Bitdeer.
The money would fund Volta Infra Holdings’ buildout of AI data centres, according to people familiar with the financing, and neither company would comment.
Renting from a bitcoin miner is now unremarkable.
It will be owned by a bitcoin miner, leased by a startup younger than most probation periods, and used by a company in San Francisco.

title: Google’s new AI transcription edits out your ‘ums’ and ‘ahs’
summary:
Google has updated Gemini Audio with new transcription capabilities that automatically detect specialized jargon and more than 85 languages.
Google says that 3.5 Transcribe “represents a major advancement from our previous transcription model, Chirp 3,” especially regarding multilingual performance and wording error rates.
Alongside 3.5 Transcribe, Google also said that 3.5 Live and 3.5 Live Experimental updates will be coming to Gemini Audio today that build on the existing speech recognition tech powering Gemini’s voice chat mode.
Gemini 3.5 Transcribe is rolling out starting today in English for all macOS Gemini app users, and the Rambler dictation feature on Android in select countries and languages.
Update, August 26th: Google also mentioned two Gemini 3.5 Live and 3.5 Live Experimental in information provided to The Verge prior to publication, but now says that only 3.5 Transcribe is being announced today.

summary:

Daniel Kirichanski of Prime Path Global argues that growth-stage companies need executive technology leadership for AI integration but not necessarily a full-time hire.

He says, “Fractional work, especially in technology, is the new wave.
It’s like a tsunami.”For founders navigating rapid growth, increasing technology complexity, and an AI landscape evolving at unprecedented speed, Fractional CTO leadership offers a new model for accessing experienced technology leadership.

summary:
Anthropic has agreed to spend $45B over six years renting AI computing power from Nscale’s flagship West Virginia data centre development, covering about 460 megawatts.
Anthropic has agreed to spend $45B renting computing power, and the landlord is British.
The six-year deal covers capacity at Nscale’s flagship data centre development in West Virginia, amounting to around 460 megawatts.
It follows a year in which Anthropic has signed compute deals with a week-old startup, with Fluidstack for $50B and with SpaceX for $45B .

But since traps like reposting AI as your homework have become so common, maybe a label like meat proxy is just what we need to raise some awareness.

title: CEO Jensen Huang went on an AI deal spree in August. Nvidia plans to invest $18 billion more this fiscal year.
summary:
In the span of a few weeks, the Nvidia CEO has committed billions to deals and investments — with more potentially right around the corner.
The spending spree shows how far Nvidia is expanding beyond chips and raises a bigger question: how much of the AI ecosystem does it want a hand in?
As Amazon, Google, and Microsoft build their own chips, Nvidia is pushing further into the infrastructure, software, and models that surround them.
On the financing front, it teamed up with Wall Street firms to raise more than $500 billion in outside funding for AI infrastructure.

title: Jensen Huang says AI data centers can fix the very grid they’re straining
summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says the AI industry needs to do "better" when it comes to data centers.
Huang said the industry needs to sell the idea that data center construction can help reindustrialize the nation.
Addressing a frequent concern, Huang said data centers could actually lower energy costs.

Greg Abbott, who is seeking reelection, imposed an effective moratorium on new data center construction until state agencies complete a comprehensive audit.

title: Judge says Pentagon's measures against Anthropic were 'illegal and baseless'
summary:
Judge says Pentagon's measures against Anthropic were 'illegal and baseless'toggle caption Jacquelyn Martin/APA federal judge has ruled in favor of artificial intelligence company Anthropic in its legal battle against the Pentagon after the government labeled the company as a supply chain risk earlier this year.
U.S. District Judge Rita Lin issued a written order Thursday night that the Pentagon acted illegally by punishing the AI company for its criticism of the Department of Defense's views on AI use.
The dispute between the AI company and the government broke out in February when President Donald Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth accused Anthropic of endangering national security and designated the company a supply chain risk.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei refused to back down over concerns the company's products could be used for mass surveillance or autonomous armed drones.
Anthropic sued the Pentagon over the supply chain risk designation in March for what it called an "unlawful campaign of retaliation" over its refusal to allow unrestricted military use of its technology.

Bill Gates says it’s time to hit the AI panic button.
The technology has crossed dangerous thresholds in biology, cybersecurity, white-collar work, and human relationships, Gates said in an interview with Semafor.
“I am in a state of shock that I’m sort of the first one saying, ‘This is crazy.

title: Greens call for temporary ban on new data centres
summary:
Zack Polanski has called for a freeze on the approval of new data centres in England because of concerns about the amount of water and energy they use.
Data centres can use significant amounts of water to cool their systems, although there are no official figures on how much water they consume in the UK.
The government said a pause would lead to the UK losing investment and being dependent on overseas computing for sensitive data processing.
There are hundreds of data centres in the UK – with plans for many more.
The amount of water data centres consume can change based on size, design and local climate - the hotter the area the more water needed to cool the equipment.

title: The US Army is betting on nuclear microreactors to keep its bases powered even if the grid goes dark
summary:
The US Army announced plans to build nuclear microreactors on five military bases as it tests whether nuclear energy can keep critical operations running if the power grid goes down.
The Army sees the technology as a potential way to ensure bases and troops can operate off-grid during a conflict.
Questions remain about the ultimate cost, which vendors will prove viable, and how widely the Army could deploy the reactors.
Army Secretary Dan Driscoll said the contracts are meant to give bases reliable power independent of potentially vulnerable external commercial grids.
Nuclear microreactors are small nuclear reactors that generate power through nuclear fission on a smaller scale.

title: Spain wants data centres on 80% renewables every hour, or no grid connection
summary:
Spain has drafted a decree that would require new data centres to source at least 80% of their electricity from renewables in every hour of operation, with loss of grid connection as the penalty for failing to comply.
The hourly requirement is the technically demanding part.
Every new megawatt requires matching renewable installations to be in place within 18 months before operation, achieved either through contracts or by building locally.
Developers who priced their models on annual renewable matching would have to redo the arithmetic or walk away from a queue position that took years to obtain.
Consultation is where the industry gets to argue, and the hourly matching requirement is the clause it will argue about.

title: ICE awards $16.7M contract to buy 6,000 pairs of gloves that deliver electric shocks
summary:
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement has awarded a $16.7 million contract to purchase 6,000 pairs of gloves that can deliver painful electric shocks, saying officers would use them to control detainees and protesters who resist.
ICE moved forward with the purchase despite opposition from civil rights advocates and Democratic members of Congress, who said ICE officers cannot be trusted to use them appropriately.
A notice published in a federal database Thursday said ICE entered into a no-bid contract to purchase the gloves from Compliant Technologies LLC, a Kentucky-based firm that manufactures them.

summary:

“Egypt is one of dozens of countries with whom we are speaking about US technology leadership on artificial intelligence,” a State Department spokesperson said.
American AI “benefits the world”, they added, and the US “stands ready to partner with countries on AI development and deployment in ways that respect sovereignty and expand capabilities”.
Malaysia is the precedentMalaysia announced a national AI system running on Huawei chips last year, on a similar scale to the Egyptian proposal.
The country’s second national AI strategy targets a 7.7% contribution to GDP by 2030, and it does not make its own chips.
